## Detect empty droplets with `DropletUtils`

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Set a seed. This can be any number. Using the same number every time ensures that a sequence of random numbers generated is the same every time you run your code.
set.seed(100)

# set `by.rank` to the max number of cells you expect
e.out <- emptyDrops(counts(sce), 
                    by.rank = as.numeric(params$expected_cells)) 

# add barcodes to a column
e.out$barcode = rownames(e.out)

# make a vector of significant barcodes
# use a false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.1%,
# meaning that no more than 0.1% of our called 
# barcodes should be empty droplets on average.
sig_barcodes <- 
  as_tibble(e.out) %>%
  filter(FDR < .001) %>% 
  pull(barcode)

```
Empty droplets often contain RNA from the ambient solution, resulting in non-zero counts after debarcoding. The `emptyDrops` function is designed to distinguish between empty droplets and cells. It does so by testing each barcode’s expression profile for significant deviation from the ambient profile. Using this method, `r length(sig_barcodes)` barcodes represent cells.

Below is a barcode rank plot, or knee plot, which shows the (log-)total UMI count for each barcode on the y-axis and the (log-)rank on the x-axis. The plot resembles a curve with a sharp "knee" or "elbow." Cells with high RNA content (likely real biological cells), are on the left side of the plot. Low-RNA-content cells (likely empty droplets or low-quality cells) are on the right side. The "knee" or transition point marks the threshold between high-quality cells and low-quality or empty droplets.

```{r}
br.out <- barcodeRanks(counts(sce))

# make the rownames a column
br.out$barcodes <- rownames(br.out)

br.df =
  as.data.frame(br.out) %>%
  mutate(keep_cells = case_when(
   barcodes %in% sig_barcodes ~ "TRUE",
   !barcodes %in% sig_barcodes ~ "FALSE"
  ))

# Making the knee plot.
ggplot(br.df, aes(x=rank, y=total)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = keep_cells)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black","red")) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=metadata(br.out)$knee,
             linetype="knee"),
             color = "dodgerblue") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=metadata(br.out)$inflection,
             linetype="inflection"),
             color = "forestgreen") +
  scale_linetype_manual(name = "legend", 
                        values = c(2, 2), 
                        guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = c("forestgreen", "dodgerblue")))) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans='log10') +
  scale_y_continuous(trans='log10') +
  xlab("Rank") +
  ylab("Total Counts")

ggsave(file = paste0(results_dir,"/", sampleID, "_kneeplot.png"))
 sce <- sce[,sig_barcodes]
```

## Identifying low quality cells

Common metrics include for identifying low quality cells include:

  * Total counts    
  * Number of expressed features (genes)   
  * Proportion of reads mapped to genes in the mitochondrial genome    
  
For each cell, we calculate these QC metrics using the `perCellQCMetrics()` function from the `scater` package.

```{r}
# Identifying the mitochondrial transcripts in our SingleCellExperiment.

# mouse mito genes start with "mt"
# human is "MT"
# change for different species
# this is a numeric vector of row numbers
# corresponding to mito genes
# NC_001626.1
all_genes = read.delim("/mnt/research/bioinformaticsCore/shared/Genomes/Petromyzon_marinus/GCF_010993605.1_kPetMar1.pri_genes.txt", header=F)

mito_genes = 
  all_genes %>% 
  filter(V1 == "NC_001626.1") %>%
  pull(V6)

mito_genes = gsub("gene ", "", mito_genes)
is.mito = which(rownames(sce) %in% mito_genes)

# get the per cell stats
stats <- perCellQCMetrics(sce,
                          subsets=list(Mito=is.mito))
```

### Summarize the stats

The total counts in each cell:
```{r}
summary(stats$sum)
```

The number of genes with at least one count in each cell:
```{r}
summary(stats$detected)
```

These are the genes on the mitochondrial chromosome, NC_001626.1.

```{r}
mito_genes
```

The percent of counts that come from mitochondria genes:
```{r}
summary(stats$subsets_Mito_percent)
```

### Filter cells with high mitochondria gene reads

```{r}
high.mito <- isOutlier(stats$subsets_Mito_percent, type="higher")
```

I propose removing every cell with percent mito > `r as.numeric(attr(high.mito, "thresholds")[2])`, which is 3 median absolute deviations (MAD) above the median percent mito. This is `r sum(high.mito)` out of `r length(high.mito)` cells.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
counts = counts(sce)
cds <- new_cell_data_set(counts,
                         cell_metadata = stats)
colData(cds)$discard = high.mito
saveRDS(cds, file = paste0(data_dir, "/", sampleID, "_cds.Rds"))
```

## Check for enrichment of known cell-type markers 

This table contains the top ~100 cluster enriched genes for each cluster after removing mitochondria genes. It is saved in `r paste0( sampleID, "_cluster_marker_genes_mito_filtered.csv")`. The markers can help us map a cluster to a cell type.

**Column descriptions**

* `gene_id` vector of gene names    
* `cell_group` character vector of the cell group to which the cell belongs   
* `marker_score` numeric vector of marker scores as the fraction expressing scaled by the specificity. The value ranges from 0 to 1.    
* `mean_expression` numeric vector of mean normalized expression of the gene in the cell group    
* `fraction_expressing` numeric vector of fraction of cells expressing the gene within the cell group   
* `specificity` numeric vector of a measure of how specific the gene's expression is to the cell group based on the Jensen-Shannon divergence. The value ranges from 0 to 1.   
* `pseudo_R2` numeric vector of pseudo R-squared values, a measure of how well the gene expression model fits the categorical data relative to the null model. The value ranges from 0 to 1.   
* `marker_test_p_value` numeric vector of likelihood ratio p-values   
* `marker_test_q_value` numeric vector of likelihood ratio q-values   

```{r, eval=FALSE}
marker_test_res <- top_markers(cds,
                               genes_to_test_per_group = 100,
                               group_cells_by="cluster", cores=8)

write.csv(marker_test_res, file = paste0(results_dir, "/", sampleID, "_cluster_marker_genes_mito_filtered.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(DT)
datatable(marker_test_res, filter = "top")
```

We'll check for the significance of the overlap between the top 100 cluster enriched genes and the supplied known cell-type markers. In the plot below, the rows represent cell types with know marker genes, and the columns represent the cell clusters. The number in each box is the number of genes shared between the top 100 cluster enriched genes for the specified clusters and the specified known cell-type markers. Each box is colored by the significance of the overlap ($-log10(FDR)$).

```{r}
# load known marker genes
library(readr)
chung_davidson_cell_type_markers <- read_csv(paste0(data_dir, "/chung_davidson_cell_type_markers.csv"))
chung_davidson_cell_type_markers = 
  chung_davidson_cell_type_markers %>%
  select(-GeneName)

marker_test_genes = 
  marker_test_res %>%
  select(gene_id, cell_group)

cluster_ol =  phyperOverlapSets(chung_davidson_cell_type_markers, 
                                marker_test_genes, nrow(genes))

write.csv(cluster_ol$intersecting.genes, file = paste0(results_dir, "/", sampleID, "_marker_gene_overlaps_mito_filtered.csv"), row.names = FALSE) 

scores = cluster_ol$pval.scores

scores = 
  scores %>%
  rename(Group1 = "CellTypes",
         Group2 = "Clusters") %>%
  group_by(CellTypes) %>%
    mutate(FDR = p.adjust(Pval, "BH"))

scores$FDR[scores$FDR > .01] = 1

plot1 =
    ggplot(scores,
           aes(Clusters, CellTypes)) + 
           geom_tile(aes(fill = -log10(FDR)), 
                     color = "light gray") +
        #Creating legend
        guides(fill=guide_colorbar(title = "-log10(FDR)",
                                   barheight = 10,
                                   barwidth = 2,
                                   default.unit = "mm")) +
        #Creating color range
        scale_fill_gradientn(colors=c("white",
                                      "#fd9668",
                                      "#f1605d",
                                      "#de4968",
                                      "#9e2f7f"),
                             guide="colorbar",
                             limits = c(0, 23)) +
        #Rotating labels
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, 
                                         hjust = 0,vjust=-0.05),
              ) +
        theme(text = element_text(size = 7),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
        geom_text(aes(label = nSharedGenes), size = 1) +
        coord_fixed()

plot1

ggsave(plot1, file = paste0(results_dir, "/", sampleID, "_overlap_heatmap_mito_filtered.png"))
```

## Ambient RNA correction with SoupX

The same library corrected for ambient RNA with SoupX. The cells are the ones
kept above: the emptyDrops calls with the high-mitochondrial cells removed, read
from `<sample>_cds_mito_filter.Rds`. Nothing more is filtered, so the corrected
library holds the same cells as the uncorrected one and the two atlases can be
compared cell for cell.

```{r}
library(scran)
library(SoupX)
```

```{r}
# droplets whose total count falls in this range, endpoints excluded, are taken
# as empty and give the soup profile (the SoupX default)
soup_range = c(0, 100)
# fewer empty droplets than this and the soup profile is too noisy to use
min_soup_droplets = 1000
rho_source = match.arg(params$rho_source, c("auto", "spermatocyte"))
# neighbors per cell in the SNN graph that gives SoupX its clusters
cluster_k  = 20
marker_file = "canonical_markers_S1_only_2026-08-14.csv"

soupx_dir = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/soupx/", sampleID)
if (!dir.exists(soupx_dir)) dir.create(soupx_dir, recursive = TRUE)
out_file  = paste0(soupx_dir, "/", sampleID, "_soupx.Rds")

gene_description = read.csv(paste0(data_dir, "/gene_descritption.csv"),
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

### Droplets and cells

The table of droplets is every barcode in the raw matrix, including the empty
ones. The table of counts is the kept cells.

```{r}
# the raw matrix read at the top, with every barcode, empty droplets included
raw_dir = paste0(data_dir, "/", sampleID, "/raw_matrix")
tod     = as(mat, "CsparseMatrix")

cds   = readRDS(paste0(data_dir, "/", sampleID, "/", sampleID,
                       "_cds_mito_filter.Rds"))
cells = colnames(cds)
stopifnot(all(cells %in% colnames(tod)),
          setequal(rownames(cds), rownames(tod)))

toc = tod[, cells]
# the kept cells' counts must be the raw counts, or the correction would be
# applied to something other than what the atlas was built on
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(Matrix::colSums(toc)),
                           unname(Matrix::colSums(counts(cds)[rownames(toc), ])))))

drop_umis   = Matrix::colSums(tod)
n_soup_drop = sum(drop_umis > soup_range[1] & drop_umis < soup_range[2])
if (n_soup_drop < min_soup_droplets)
  stop("only ", n_soup_drop, " droplets have between ", soup_range[1], " and ",
       soup_range[2], " counts. The soup profile needs empty droplets; check ",
       "that ", raw_dir, " is the unfiltered matrix.")
```

`r paste0(format(ncol(tod), big.mark = ","), " droplets in the raw matrix, ", format(ncol(toc), big.mark = ","), " of them cells. ", format(n_soup_drop, big.mark = ","), " droplets hold between ", soup_range[1], " and ", soup_range[2], " counts and give the soup profile.")`

### Clusters

SoupX shares information within clusters when it subtracts, because a single
count in a single cell cannot be told apart from soup. The clusters are a
quick SNN clustering of this library alone. They only group similar cells for
the correction and are not the atlas clusters.

```{r}
soup_sce = SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = toc))
soup_sce = logNormCounts(soup_sce)
soup_dec = modelGeneVar(soup_sce)
set.seed(100)
soup_sce = runPCA(soup_sce, subset_row = getTopHVGs(soup_dec, prop = 0.1),
                  ncomponents = 30)
soup_graph = buildSNNGraph(soup_sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = cluster_k)
set.seed(100)
soup_clusters = setNames(as.character(igraph::cluster_louvain(soup_graph)$membership),
                         colnames(soup_sce))

datatable(as.data.frame(table(cluster = soup_clusters)) %>%
            dplyr::rename(n_cells = Freq),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

### Soup profile

```{r}
sc = SoupChannel(tod, toc, calcSoupProfile = FALSE)
sc = estimateSoup(sc, soupRange = soup_range)
sc = setClusters(sc, soup_clusters)
rm(tod, soup_sce); invisible(gc())

soup_top = sc$soupProfile %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(est)) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 50) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_description, by = "Gene") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Gene, WangGeneID, description,
                   pct_of_soup = signif(100 * est, 3))

write.csv(soup_top, file = paste0(soupx_dir, "/", sampleID, "_soup_profile_top50.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(soup_top, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
          options = list(pageLength = 15))
```

The fifty genes contributing most to the soup. A library dominated by one cell
type has that cell type's transcripts at the top.

### Contamination fraction

Two estimates of the contamination fraction, rho, the share of a cell's
counts that come from the soup.

* **auto**: SoupX's `autoEstCont`. It finds genes abundant in the soup that are
  also specific to a few clusters, and estimates rho from the clusters that do
  not express them.
* **spermatocyte**: the curated spermatocyte markers, which no somatic cell
  expresses. This is the direct probe for the male library, whose soup is mostly
  spermatocyte transcripts.

For the spermatocyte set, `estimateNonExpressingCells` excludes every cluster
in which any cell shows real expression, and rho is fitted on the clusters left.

```{r}
curated = read.csv(paste0(data_dir, "/", marker_file), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spermatocyte_genes = curated$loc_id[curated$CellTypeMarkerSet == "Spermatocytes"]

marker_sets = list(spermatocyte = intersect(spermatocyte_genes, rownames(toc)))

# rho from a named gene set; NA where no cluster can be assumed not to
# express it
rho_from_set = function(set_name) {
  gs = marker_sets[set_name]
  if (length(gs[[1]]) == 0) return(c(rho = NA, low = NA, high = NA, n_cells = 0))
  ute = estimateNonExpressingCells(sc, gs, clusters = soup_clusters)
  if (sum(ute) == 0) return(c(rho = NA, low = NA, high = NA, n_cells = 0))
  fit = calculateContaminationFraction(sc, gs, useToEst = ute,
                                       verbose = FALSE, forceAccept = TRUE)
  c(rho = unique(fit$metaData$rho), low = unique(fit$metaData$rhoLow),
    high = unique(fit$metaData$rhoHigh), n_cells = sum(ute))
}

auto_fit = tryCatch(autoEstCont(sc, doPlot = FALSE, verbose = FALSE,
                                forceAccept = TRUE),
                    error = function(e) { message("autoEstCont failed: ",
                                                  conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

rho_tab = dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(estimate = "auto",
             rho  = if (is.null(auto_fit)) NA else auto_fit$fit$rhoEst,
             low  = if (is.null(auto_fit)) NA else auto_fit$fit$rhoFWHM[1],
             high = if (is.null(auto_fit)) NA else auto_fit$fit$rhoFWHM[2],
             n_genes = if (is.null(auto_fit)) NA else length(auto_fit$fit$markersUsed$gene),
             n_cells = NA),
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(marker_sets), function(s) {
    r = rho_from_set(s)
    data.frame(estimate = s, rho = r[["rho"]], low = r[["low"]],
               high = r[["high"]], n_genes = length(marker_sets[[s]]),
               n_cells = r[["n_cells"]])
  }))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(applied = estimate == rho_source)

write.csv(rho_tab, file = paste0(soupx_dir, "/", sampleID, "_rho_estimates.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(rho_tab %>% dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(rho, low, high), ~ signif(., 3))),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", ordering = FALSE))

rho_used = rho_tab$rho[rho_tab$estimate == rho_source]
if (is.na(rho_used))
  stop("the ", rho_source, " estimate could not be made for ", sampleID,
       ". Knit again with the rho_source parameter set to another estimate; ",
       "the table above shows which ones exist.")
```

`r paste0("**rho = ", signif(100 * rho_used, 3), " percent is applied, from the ", rho_source, " estimate.** ")``r if (!is.null(auto_fit)) paste0("For auto the interval is the posterior's full width at half maximum, over ", length(auto_fit$fit$markersUsed$gene), " marker genes. ") else "autoEstCont did not return an estimate. "`For spermatocyte it is the 95 percent confidence interval of the Poisson fit, and `n_cells` is the number of cells it was fitted on.

### Correction

```{r}
sc  = setContaminationFraction(sc, rho_used)
out = adjustCounts(sc, roundToInt = TRUE, verbose = 0)
stopifnot(identical(dim(out), dim(toc)), identical(colnames(out), colnames(toc)))

before = Matrix::colSums(toc)
after  = Matrix::colSums(out)

removed = data.frame(cluster = soup_clusters[colnames(toc)],
                     before = before, after = after) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_removed = 100 * (before - after) / before) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_cells = dplyr::n(),
                   median_counts = round(median(before)),
                   median_pct_removed = round(median(pct_removed), 2),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(median_pct_removed))

datatable(removed, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

`r paste0(signif(100 * (1 - sum(after) / sum(before)), 3), " percent of the library's counts are removed. A fixed amount of soup is a larger share of a shallow cell, so the clusters with the lowest counts lose the most.")`

The genes losing the largest share of their counts. These are the genes whose
expression outside their own cell type was mostly soup.

```{r}
gene_change = data.frame(Gene   = rownames(toc),
                         before = Matrix::rowSums(toc),
                         after  = Matrix::rowSums(out)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(before >= 100) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_removed = round(100 * (before - after) / before, 1)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(pct_removed)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_description, by = "Gene") %>%
  dplyr::select(Gene, WangGeneID, description, before, after, pct_removed)

write.csv(gene_change, file = paste0(soupx_dir, "/", sampleID, "_gene_counts_removed.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(head(gene_change, 50), rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
          options = list(pageLength = 15))
```

### Probe genes before and after

Mean counts per cell of the spermatocyte markers, SYCP3 and PIWIL1,
by cluster. In a cluster that does not express a gene, the corrected value
should fall toward zero. In one that does, it should hold.

```{r}
probe = c(list(SYCP3 = "SYCP3", PIWIL1 = "PIWIL1"), marker_sets)
probe = probe[vapply(probe, function(g) any(g %in% rownames(toc)), logical(1))]

probe_tab = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(probe), function(p) {
  g = intersect(probe[[p]], rownames(toc))
  data.frame(probe   = p,
             cluster = soup_clusters[colnames(toc)],
             before  = Matrix::colSums(toc[g, , drop = FALSE]),
             after   = Matrix::colSums(out[g, , drop = FALSE]))
})) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(probe, cluster) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_cells = dplyr::n(),
                   mean_before = round(mean(before), 3),
                   mean_after  = round(mean(after), 3),
                   pct_cells_before = round(100 * mean(before > 0), 1),
                   pct_cells_after  = round(100 * mean(after > 0), 1),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(probe, dplyr::desc(mean_before))

write.csv(probe_tab, file = paste0(soupx_dir, "/", sampleID, "_probe_genes_before_after.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(probe_tab, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
          options = list(pageLength = 20))
```

### Export

The corrected counts, with the per-cell QC carried from the uncorrected object,
so `01_atlas_soupx.Rmd` can read it in place of `<sample>_cds_mito_filter.Rds`.

```{r}
cd = colData(cds)
cd$soupx_cluster = soup_clusters[colnames(cds)]
cd$soupx_rho     = rho_used
cd$soupx_counts_before = before[colnames(cds)]

corrected = SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = out[rownames(cds), colnames(cds)]),
                                 colData = cd)
metadata(corrected)$soupx = list(rho = rho_used, rho_source = rho_source,
                                 rho_estimates = rho_tab,
                                 soup_range = soup_range)
saveRDS(corrected, file = out_file)
```
